column12: Purpose in the project

column11: Dual-core ESP32-S3, 16MB flash, 8MB PSRAM, WiFi + Bluetooth 5, USB-C, JST LiPo socket with onboard charger, camera interface
column12: Runs the robot's software. PSRAM holds animation frames for smooth eyes and games; WiFi handles online mode and ESP-NOW handles robot-to-robot messages; the onboard charger removes the need for a separate charging module; the camera interface keeps a later upgrade possible.
Shows the animated eyes, expressions and games. Colour output gives expressive faces, the size suits the robot's face, and the SPI interface needs only a few pins. ST7789 has wide library support.

column11: 3.7V single cell, 3000mAh, built-in protection circuit, approx. 73 x 49 x 6 mm
column12: Powers the robot for long play sessions. The thin flat shape fits behind the display, the protection circuit guards against over-charge, over-discharge and short circuit, and it charges through the board's USB-C port.

column11: MAX98357A: I2S digital input, 3W Class D amplifier. INMP441: I2S digital MEMS microphone. Header pins pre-soldered
column12: Gives the robot a voice and hearing. The I2S amplifier drives the speaker directly from digital audio with no separate DAC and the digital microphone gives clean sound input for sound reactions.
Plays sounds, beeps and voice. Its 4 ohm / 3W rating matches the amplifier's output, and the compact round shape fits behind a grille in the robot's back.
Detects shaking, tilting and being picked up, so the robot can react with expressions and sounds.

column4: TTP223 capacitive touch module, SKU TIFSS0094
column12: Lets the robot respond to being touched on the head, chest and side. Works through a thin plastic wall, so the sensors can sit hidden inside the case. One spare included.
Turns the robot on and off by breaking the battery connection. One spare included.

column4: 2 mm pitch 2-pin JST cable with connector, pack of 10, SKU TIFCW0050
column12: Connects the battery to the controller board's JST socket and lets the battery be unplugged or replaced without soldering to the board.
